notes: AGENCIES: 19 agencies are listed together as 'authoring and co-sealing agencies', and the text does not say which role each one has. Trailing numerals are footnote markers, not parts of names or IDs: 1-11 after the non-Five-Eyes agencies, '12' in 'Enterprise 12 framework', and '13' after CVE-2008-4128. CVEs: the text does not map either CVE to a specific product. The product field therefore lists the three targets named in the sentence (Cisco devices; Cisco’s Smart Install (SMI) functionality; web portals to manage network devices). Per the instructions they are not repeated under affected_products. Credit models that list them as affected products or map a CVE within this set. Mapping CVE-2018-0171 specifically to Smart Install uses outside knowledge but is consistent with the text. Both CVEs are 'previously exploited' and secondary to SNMP scanning. ACTORS: Salt Typhoon is mentioned ONLY as another actor whose TTPs overlap. It is not an alias, unit or attribution, so listing it as this actor is an error. The six industry names are 'threat group names commonly used within the cybersecurity community related to this activity', with a 1:1-correlation caveat. 'Russian Government Cyber Actors' appears only inside the title of the referenced FBI PSA. TOOLS: no malware or tool names appear, so malware_tools is empty. SNMP and TFTP are protocols, recorded as technologies; a model listing them as tools is not hallucinating. 'config.bkp' and 'output.txt' are file names (IOC-like). Actor infrastructure (proxies, spoofed IP addresses, actor-controlled leased VPS) is not a target. DATES: there are no calendar dates and no publication date; 'decade-plus' is the only temporal expression. REGIONS: the only geographic scope is 'worldwide'. The sector names follow US critical-infrastructure terminology, but no country is stated, so listing 'United States' as the target region is inference. REFERENCED DOCUMENTS (not items): the FBI PSA 'Russian Government Cyber Actors Targeting Networking Devices, Critical Infrastructure' and the companion PDF 'Improve Router Hygiene to Protect Against Russian State-Sponsored Targeting'. 'MITRE DEFEND TM version 1.4.0' (sic, D3FEND) and ATT&CK v19 are frameworks, not tools. KEY TECHNIQUE (not a schema item): SNMP Set-Requests from spoofed IPs, carrying OIDs that make devices copy their configuration and TFTP it to actor-controlled VPS or compromised FTP servers, exploiting common/default community strings.
